subject: geom_text in forest plots - some text is not appearing on the chart

messages.author: dc2f7ab6529ad6b0
messages.subject: geom_text in forest plots - some text is not appearing on the chart
parts:
Hello,
 
My goal is to  update forest plots that I had earlier prepared with help from Dennis Murphy on this forum  - Thanks to Dennis. This time I am trying to update the earlier plots by adding 11 rows for each of the 3 facets.  
 
The current plots involve estimates of hazarad ratios, LCL, and UCL associated with 11 predictors from 3 models  for 3 age groups (=99 rows).   Although I am getting all the 99 plots, the issue is that the geom_text portion of the code is not working (i.e., I am missing the text associated with some of the horizontal lines).   The reproducible example is  attached.    Sorry, the .png file is too large to attach.
 
I would be grateful if someone could give me hints/advice on how to resolve the issue.
 
Thanks,
 
Pradip
 
 
##############  below is the minimal code, full reproducible example example is attached   #############################
 
p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=xcovariate_f, y=or, ymin=lc, ymax=uc))+
  geom_pointrange(size = 0.8)+
  geom_hline(aes(x=0), lty=2) +
  geom_text(y = 0.2, aes(label= string.est,
                         x = as.numeric(data$xcovariate_f) - 0.5),
            size = 2.5, hjust = 0, colour="black")+
  facet_wrap(~ age_cat_f)+
  coord_flip()+
  xlab (" ")+
  ylab("Adjusted hazard ratio (95% CI) ")+
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_rect(colour="black",
                                        fill='white')
  )

messages.subject: Re: geom_text in forest plots - some text is not appearing on the chart
parts:
A few modifications to your code produce what I think you want:

ggplot(data, aes(y=xcovariate_f, x=or, xmin=lc, xmax=uc))+
geom_errorbarh(size = 1, height = 0)+
geom_point(size = 2.5) +
geom_vline(aes(y=0), lty=2) +
geom_text(x = 0.2, aes(label= string.est,
y = as.numeric(xcovariate_f) - 0.5),
labs(x = "Adjusted hazard ratio (95% CI) ", y = NULL)+

theme_bw() +
theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),
panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
strip.background = element_rect(colour="black",
fill='white'))

The main culprit was the reference to data$xcovariate_f in
geom_text(). I also changed geom_pointrange() to a combination of
geom_errorbarh() and geom_point() to avoid the need for a
coord_flip(). As a result, the x's need to be changed to y's and vice
versa in the plot code.

Dennis

Hello Ista- Thank you for expressing your views/comments (i.e., distraction from the plot because of all estimates presented underneath the plot).  One solution could be presenting the entire chart in landscape format and inserting the estimates at a constant place to the right of each plot.
 
Dennis - Any comments? Thanks,
 
Questions:
1) What do you think about rotating the graph to a landscape format?
2) What options would I use to rotate the graph in landscape - \documentclass{article} \begin{document} <<out.extra='angle=90'>>= (in knitr)?
3) How to tweak the existing code to insert the estimates in a column to the right of each facet?
 
Any advice would be appreciated.
 
regards,
 
Pradip
